classification.difficultyReason: Transform expanded quadratics into vertex form, determine real intercepts and coordinate these results in a sketch. The student must organise the taught procedures and interpret whether the parabola crosses, touches or misses the x-axis.

content.prompt: Sketch the following parabolas, labelling the turning points and any intercepts.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=x^2+2x+1-1+6\\y&=(x+1)^2+5\end{align*}$$
The turning point is $(-1,5)$. When $x=0$, $y=6$, so the $y$-intercept is $(0,6)$. Since $(x+1)^2+5\geq5$, there are no $x$-intercepts. Sketch an upward-opening parabola through these features.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5a; answer PDF page 54, bottom left
spec.description: Upward parabola with labelled vertex and y-intercept; no x-intercepts, ticks or grid.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=x^2-6x+9-9+10\\y&=(x-3)^2+1\end{align*}$$
The turning point is $(3,1)$. When $x=0$, $y=10$, giving $(0,10)$. Since $(x-3)^2+1\geq1$, there are no $x$-intercepts. Sketch an upward-opening parabola.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5b; answer PDF page 54, bottom left
spec.description: Upward parabola with minimum above the x-axis and labelled vertex and y-intercept.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=x^2-4x+4-4+7\\y&=(x-2)^2+3\end{align*}$$
The turning point is $(2,3)$. When $x=0$, $y=7$, giving $(0,7)$. Since $(x-2)^2+3\geq3$, there are no $x$-intercepts. Sketch an upward-opening parabola.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5c; answer PDF page 54, right column
spec.description: Upward parabola with labelled minimum and y-intercept above the x-axis.

answer.short: Turning point $(-1,-4)$; intercepts $(-3,0)$, $(1,0)$ and $(0,-3)$. Opens upwards.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=x^2+2x+1-1-3\\y&=(x+1)^2-4\end{align*}$$
The turning point is $(-1,-4)$. When $x=0$, $y=-3$.

For the $x$-intercepts:
$$\begin{align*}(x+1)^2-4&=0\\(x+1)^2&=4\\x+1&=\pm2\\x&=-3\text{ or }1\end{align*}$$
Sketch an upward-opening parabola through $(-3,0)$, $(1,0)$ and $(0,-3)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5d; answer PDF page 54, right column
spec.description: Upward parabola with vertex and all three intercept points labelled.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=(x+2)^2\end{align*}$$
The turning point is $(-2,0)$. When $x=0$, $y=4$.
$$\begin{align*}(x+2)^2&=0\\x&=-2\end{align*}$$
The curve touches the $x$-axis at $(-2,0)$ and opens upwards.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5e; answer PDF page 54, right column
spec.description: Upward parabola tangent to the x-axis at its labelled vertex.

answer.short: Turning point $(4,-36)$; intercepts $(-2,0)$, $(10,0)$ and $(0,-20)$. Opens upwards.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=x^2-8x+16-16-20\\y&=(x-4)^2-36\end{align*}$$
The turning point is $(4,-36)$. When $x=0$, $y=-20$.
$$\begin{align*}(x-4)^2-36&=0\\(x-4)^2&=36\\x-4&=\pm6\\x&=-2\text{ or }10\end{align*}$$
Sketch an upward-opening parabola through $(-2,0)$, $(10,0)$ and $(0,-20)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5f; answer PDF page 54, right column
spec.description: Upward parabola with labelled vertex, two roots and y-intercept; axes have independent scales.

answer.short: Turning point $(-1,-2)$; intercepts $(-1-\sqrt2,0)$, $(-1+\sqrt2,0)$ and $(0,-1)$. Opens upwards.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=x^2+2x+1-1-1\\y&=(x+1)^2-2\end{align*}$$
The turning point is $(-1,-2)$. When $x=0$, $y=-1$.
$$\begin{align*}(x+1)^2-2&=0\\(x+1)^2&=2\\x+1&=\pm\sqrt2\\x&=-1\pm\sqrt2\end{align*}$$
Sketch an upward-opening parabola through the intercepts $(-1-\sqrt2,0)$, $(-1+\sqrt2,0)$ and $(0,-1)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5g; answer PDF page 54, right column
spec.description: Upward parabola with exact surd root labels, vertex and y-intercept.

answer.short: Turning point $(3,-12)$; intercepts $(3-2\sqrt3,0)$, $(3+2\sqrt3,0)$ and $(0,-3)$. Opens upwards.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=x^2-6x+9-9-3\\y&=(x-3)^2-12\end{align*}$$
The turning point is $(3,-12)$. When $x=0$, $y=-3$.
$$\begin{align*}(x-3)^2-12&=0\\(x-3)^2&=12\\x-3&=\pm2\sqrt3\\x&=3\pm2\sqrt3\end{align*}$$
Sketch an upward-opening parabola through the intercepts $(3-2\sqrt3,0)$, $(3+2\sqrt3,0)$ and $(0,-3)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5h; answer PDF page 54, right column
spec.description: Upward parabola with exact surd root labels, vertex and y-intercept.

answer.short: Turning point $(-5,-5)$; intercepts $(-5-\sqrt5,0)$, $(-5+\sqrt5,0)$ and $(0,20)$. Opens upwards.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=x^2+10x+25-25+20\\y&=(x+5)^2-5\end{align*}$$
The turning point is $(-5,-5)$. When $x=0$, $y=20$.
$$\begin{align*}(x+5)^2-5&=0\\(x+5)^2&=5\\x+5&=\pm\sqrt5\\x&=-5\pm\sqrt5\end{align*}$$
Sketch an upward-opening parabola through the intercepts $(-5-\sqrt5,0)$, $(-5+\sqrt5,0)$ and $(0,20)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5i; answer PDF page 54, right column
spec.description: Upward parabola with exact root labels, vertex and positive y-intercept.

answer.short: Turning point $(-\frac52,-\frac{49}{4})$; intercepts $(-6,0)$, $(1,0)$ and $(0,-6)$. Opens upwards.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=x^2+5x+\frac{25}{4}-\frac{25}{4}-6\\y&=\left(x+\frac52\right)^2-\frac{49}{4}\end{align*}$$
The turning point is $(-\frac52,-\frac{49}{4})$. When $x=0$, $y=-6$.
$$\begin{align*}\left(x+\frac52\right)^2-\frac{49}{4}&=0\\\left(x+\frac52\right)^2&=\frac{49}{4}\\x+\frac52&=\pm\frac72\\x&=-6\text{ or }1\end{align*}$$
Sketch an upward-opening parabola through $(-6,0)$, $(1,0)$ and $(0,-6)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5j; answer PDF page 54, bottom right
spec.description: Upward parabola with exact fractional vertex and all intercepts labelled.

answer.short: Turning point $(\frac32,-\frac{49}{4})$; intercepts $(-2,0)$, $(5,0)$ and $(0,-10)$. Opens upwards.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=x^2-3x+\frac94-\frac94-10\\y&=\left(x-\frac32\right)^2-\frac{49}{4}\end{align*}$$
The turning point is $(\frac32,-\frac{49}{4})$. When $x=0$, $y=-10$.
$$\begin{align*}\left(x-\frac32\right)^2-\frac{49}{4}&=0\\\left(x-\frac32\right)^2&=\frac{49}{4}\\x-\frac32&=\pm\frac72\\x&=-2\text{ or }5\end{align*}$$
Sketch an upward-opening parabola through $(-2,0)$, $(5,0)$ and $(0,-10)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5k; answer PDF page 55, top left
spec.description: Upward parabola with exact fractional vertex and all intercepts labelled.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=x^2-x+\frac14-\frac14+1\\y&=\left(x-\frac12\right)^2+\frac34\end{align*}$$
The turning point is $(\frac12,\frac34)$. When $x=0$, $y=1$, giving $(0,1)$. Since $y\geq\frac34$, there are no $x$-intercepts. Sketch an upward-opening parabola.

The turning point is $(-\frac32,\frac74)$. When $x=0$, $y=4$, giving $(0,4)$. Since $y\geq\frac74$, there are no $x$-intercepts. Sketch an upward-opening parabola.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5m; answer PDF page 55, left column
spec.description: Upward parabola with fractional positive minimum and labelled y-intercept.

answer.short: Turning point $(\frac52,-\frac{13}{4})$; intercepts $(\frac{5-\sqrt{13}}2,0)$, $(\frac{5+\sqrt{13}}2,0)$ and $(0,3)$. Opens upwards.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=x^2-5x+\frac{25}{4}-\frac{25}{4}+3\\y&=\left(x-\frac52\right)^2-\frac{13}{4}\end{align*}$$
The turning point is $(\frac52,-\frac{13}{4})$. When $x=0$, $y=3$.
$$\begin{align*}\left(x-\frac52\right)^2-\frac{13}{4}&=0\\\left(x-\frac52\right)^2&=\frac{13}{4}\\x-\frac52&=\pm\frac{\sqrt{13}}2\\x&=\frac{5\pm\sqrt{13}}2\end{align*}$$
Sketch an upward-opening parabola through the intercepts $(\frac{5-\sqrt{13}}2,0)$, $(\frac{5+\sqrt{13}}2,0)$ and $(0,3)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5n; answer PDF page 55, left column

answer.short: Turning point $(-\frac72,-\frac{41}{4})$; intercepts $(\frac{-7-\sqrt{41}}2,0)$, $(\frac{-7+\sqrt{41}}2,0)$ and $(0,2)$. Opens upwards.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=x^2+7x+\frac{49}{4}-\frac{49}{4}+2\\y&=\left(x+\frac72\right)^2-\frac{41}{4}\end{align*}$$
The turning point is $(-\frac72,-\frac{41}{4})$. When $x=0$, $y=2$.
$$\begin{align*}\left(x+\frac72\right)^2-\frac{41}{4}&=0\\\left(x+\frac72\right)^2&=\frac{41}{4}\\x+\frac72&=\pm\frac{\sqrt{41}}2\\x&=\frac{-7\pm\sqrt{41}}2\end{align*}$$
Sketch an upward-opening parabola through the intercepts $(\frac{-7-\sqrt{41}}2,0)$, $(\frac{-7+\sqrt{41}}2,0)$ and $(0,2)$.
